newsitem.title: SPAIN: Aerolineas Argentinas makes Q1 op profit - Iberia.
newsitem.headline: Aerolineas Argentinas makes Q1 op profit - Iberia.

text.p: Aerolineas Argentinas made a first quarter operating profit of $8.2 million compared with a loss of $2.9 million in the same period in 1996, sources at managing company Iberia said on Wednesday.

During a trip to Madrid to present Aerolineas' results, chairman Manuel Moran told Iberia that the Argentine airline's sales rose 15 percent in the quarter, while productivity was up 13 percent, sources told Reuters.
"From these results Iberia thinks the outlook for the airline is fair," one source said.

Aerolineas' passenger load factor was 70 percent over the period, while passenger kilometres grew by eight percent. Iberia sources gave no comparative figures but said full results would be published on Thursday.

As regards future shareholder changes, one source said talks with American Airlines and Continental Airlines on the possibility of buying a stake in Aerolineas should conclude in the next two to three weeks.
"One or the other will take a 20 percent stake which may or may not include involvement in the management of the airline," a source said.
Iberia currently holds a 10 percent stake in Aerolineas and controls the airline. "Iberia may eventually increase that stake to 20 percent," a source said.
Aerolineas remains Iberia's only long-term investment in Latin America.

Chilean airline Ladeco said in April that Iberia would sell its 38 percent stake in the carrier, and shareholders in Venezuela's Viasa, including Iberia, agreed to liquidate the loss-making airline within a year.
